correctness.rationale: The scalar derivative is cos(s)(1+3c sin²s); maximizing u(1+3c−3cu²) gives the exact q and minimizers stated. Signed diagonal dominance and nonsingularity give SPD K. Symmetric similarity, a positive lower derivative bound and degree one prove global invertibility. Taylor descent excludes other fixed/periodic/nonwandering points: near any noncritical point, one step decreases the potential by more than its variation on a sufficiently small neighborhood. It also makes g(F^nz)→0; vanishing steps and separation of the finite critical set imply convergence. The fixed-point inertia determines the index. For transversality, a nonzero annihilator of the two tangents propagates by the adjoint, contracting toward each end on the dual normals to the appropriate stable/unstable manifolds. At its global coordinate maximum some attaining row has strictly positive signed K action: equality in all attaining rows would separate those rows from the smaller coordinates and annihilate a nonzero vector in an SPD principal submatrix. One backward adjoint equation then places that coordinate in the negative-derivative slab, whose forward invariance follows from scalar monotonicity and diagonal dominance at the endpoints. Equality in the forward maximum bound forces the same signed maximum at every later time, contradicting decay. Positive-step descent remains strict at the first singular step off the corners, so the eight critical configurations really are nonfixed on the torus. For every hλq≥1 the required derivative value occurs between π/2 and a minimizing phase, yielding a singular diagonal configuration. At the star ceiling, the two nonnegative quadratic forms force the kernel vector along the all-ones vector and all the scalar derivatives to equal −q; this gives exactly rank two at each listed point. At c=1/6 the scalar contact coefficient is 3/8 at order four; away from the transition the minima are nondegenerate. At c>1/6 the sink multipliers at the ceiling lie strictly in (0,1).
residual_risks: Finite checker inspected, not replayed; it does not verify transversality or exhaust the torus. The statement is for h>0 and does not classify above-ceiling dynamics.

originality.rationale: The pure-sine sharp interval and maximum-adjoint method are prior, as are the graph-based general-law descent and sufficient invertibility estimates. The distinct contribution is the proved extension of transversality throughout the exact shape-dependent interval for every c≥0 and the full star critical locus with its one-to-eight switch while the sink is still hyperbolic. The relevant published structural stability result does include small interaction-law perturbations, but only near an individual sine map, not uniformly to the exact boundary. No checked matching theorem dominates the combined new conclusions.
residual_risks: A wider result for arbitrary coupled odd unimodal laws using invariant slabs could cover the extension. The bounded source check is not a historical priority certification.

value.rationale: The result separates loss of the diffeomorphism regime from loss of sink hyperbolicity. Its exact first-failure locus changes from one equilibrium to eight off-equilibrium configurations, while the global transversality result holds right up to the shape-dependent boundary. This provides a natural sharp boundary beyond a local perturbation statement.
residual_risks: The eight-point phenomenon is proved for the specified star, not for every signed diagonally dominant matrix or arbitrary nonlinear oscillator law.
